subject: CSDS
title: Programming in Java
description: An in-depth survey of modern programming language features, computer programming and algorithmic problem solving with an emphasis on the Java language. Computers and code compilation; conditional statements, subprograms, loops, methods; object-oriented design, inheritance and polymorphism, abstract classes and interfaces; types, type systems, generic types, abstract data types, strings, arrays, linked lists; software development, modular code design, unit testing; strings, text and file I/O; GUI components, GUI event handling; threads; comparison of Java to C, C++, and C#. Note: Credit given for only one (1) of CSDS 132 or CSDS 134.
notes: CWRU: CSDS 134 & CSDS 235 (Programming in Python, then The Java Programming Language) may replace it.
plan: Sample Plan of Study, Computer Science BS, 2026-2027 CWRU General Bulletin

matches.match_rationale: First course in the plan; no prerequisite. Programming and algorithmic problem solving in Java.
matches.notes: It goes further than most CS1 courses (object-oriented design, generics, linked lists, unit testing, threads), so it may also cover part of intro-programming-2.

subject: ENGR
title: Impact of Engineering on Society
description: As engineers, we design and implement technical solutions with the goal of improving people's lives, locally and globally. However, the technical solutions can have disparate impacts, in that they are beneficial to some people but less beneficial, or even detrimental, to others. What are our ethical and professional responsibilities to understand, consider, and perhaps address the disparate impacts of our work on the affected local and/or global populations?
plan: Sample Plan of Study, Computer Science BS, 2026-2027 CWRU General Bulletin

matches.match_rationale: Engineering ethics and professional responsibility for the societal impacts of technical work.
matches.notes: About engineering in general, not computing (no privacy, intellectual property, or security), so partial.
